subject.title: [Feature]: Support to edit system prompt template

question: Should OpenClaw expose editable OpenClaw-owned system prompt sections such as Safety, Tool Call Style, OpenClaw Control, and Self-Update, and should that surface be workspace-file-backed, schema/config-backed, or rejected in favor of existing hooks and overlays?
rationale: The request changes model-facing safety guidance and prompt precedence instead of repairing a broken existing contract, so automation cannot choose the permanent product and security boundary safely.

options.title: Approve scoped section overrides
options.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, auditability, security docs, and prompt regression tests.

options.title: Reject core section overrides
options.body: Keep OpenClaw-owned sections fixed and document before_prompt_build, provider overlays, channel prompts, and bootstrap files as the supported customization paths.

options.title: Defer to narrower tracks
options.body: Let identity-line, config-rules, or user-prompt replacement issues proceed independently while keeping broad Safety/template editing unresolved.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped section overrides
recommendation.body: Add a narrow named-section override model with explicit edit authority, precedence, auditability, security docs, and prompt regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on provider-owned prompt contributions and the OpenClaw-owned prompt boundary this decision would change.
